pending_commit.commit_message: tast: Remove the build subcommand. Actually the subcommand was not working at all because cfg.Logger is nil: panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference [signal SIGSEGV: segmentation violation code=0x1 addr=0x50 pc=0x551472] Even though we can fix the bug, the build subcommand has not been loved because of its difficult interface. For example, the command to simply build the cros bundle was as long as: tast build -workspaces \ $HOME/trunk/src/platform/tast-tests:$HOME/trunk/src/platform/tast:/usr/lib/gopath \ chromiumos/tast/local/bundles/cros /tmp/ We might want to introduce a better interface in the future, but for now, let us remove the subcommand entirely for the sake of maintainability. eclass: add the cros-bazel eclass. Chromium OS requires complex behavior from Bazel; in particular, cross- compilation support for a variety of architectures. This change adds a wrapper eclass 'cros-bazel' containing initial cross-compilation logic. This logic is added directly to the Bazel eclass since we can't yet guarantee the generality of our approach. However, we are confident that it works for our motivating case (TensorFlow), and doesn't impact Bazel behavior in other cases. See crrev.com/c/1679813 for an alternative approach (forking bazel.eclass) that was abandoned. TEST="emerge-chell tensorflow && emerge-kevin tensorflow && emerge-kevin64 tensorflow" BUG=chromium:955950 Change-Id: Id7b6c3d26081be08e3d17ffbc3866e9bab4ac786 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1679800 Tested-by: Michael Martis <martis@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Michael Martis <martis@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrew Moylan <amoylan@chromium.org>
